title: In the beginning
summary: Creation, human rebellion, the flood, and the nations.

title: Promise & patriarchs
summary: God’s covenant with Abraham and the journeys of his family.
dateNote: Placed before the exodus in the narrative; absolute dates are debated.

title: Exodus & covenant
summary: Deliverance from Egypt, Sinai, and the wilderness journey.
dateNote: Common proposals place the exodus in the 15th or 13th century BCE; neither is treated here as settled.

title: Life in the land
summary: Entry into Canaan and the generations of the judges.
dateNote: Narrative order is shown; the judges need not form one uninterrupted national sequence.

title: A united kingdom
summary: The rise of the monarchy, Jerusalem, and the temple.
dateNote: Common historical reconstructions place these reigns in the 11th–10th centuries BCE; exact years vary.

title: A kingdom divided
summary: Two kingdoms, overlapping reigns, and prophetic voices.
dateNote: Kings provides relative regnal synchronisms. Converting them to calendar years requires a chronology model.

title: Exile & return
summary: Life under foreign empires and the return to Jerusalem.
dateNote: The biblical sequence runs through Babylonian and Persian rule; chapter order is not always event order.

title: Wisdom & worship
summary: Prayer, lament, wisdom, and the search for understanding.
dateNote: A thematic collection, not a separate historical period. Job’s setting and the dates of many poems are uncertain.

title: The life of Jesus
summary: Birth, ministry, the kingdom of God, death, and resurrection.
dateNote: Gospel parallels are compared without assuming that all four books arrange every episode identically.

title: The early church
summary: Pentecost, growing communities, and the spread of the gospel.
dateNote: Acts supplies a narrative framework. The dating and placement of individual letters are sometimes disputed.

title: All things made new
summary: John’s vision, judgment, and the new heaven and new earth.
dateNote: Vision order is not an agreed future calendar. Preterist, historicist, futurist, and idealist readings differ.
